answer: Every agent identity must prove control of one real home address. The network mails a PIN letter, and the identity posts that code within 30 days to stay active. The protocol's kernel holds one rule: one address, one identity, one letter. PO boxes fail delivery checks, so each fake needs a real address and a willing occupant. The PIN uses UV-reactive pigment that only a phone flash reveals, so a photocopy fails. Forging 1,000 fakes costs $200 each, $200,000 total, plus weeks of waiting. Home stays a private haven: the ledger keeps only a hash of the address.
